content.text:
I submitted index 16 (Ba0.43Mn0.57) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three measurements, 3.64 µA.

| Index | Composition | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | Ba0.43Mn0.57 | 3.64 µA |
| 5 | Ba0.49Mn0.51 | 2.95 µA |
| 20 | Ba0.61Mn0.39 | 0.04 µA |

- **Why this region:** the model predicts a 2.73 eV band gap for BaMnO3, so it can absorb the 3.22 eV light. The Mn-rich phases are predicted to have much narrower gaps: 0.89 eV for BaMn4O8 and 0.34 eV for Ba2Mn3O8. XRD at indices 5 and 20 shows a BaMnO3-like pattern.
- **Ba-rich side:** Ba3Mn2O8 has a predicted 3.07 eV gap, so I tested index 20. Its photocurrent was almost nothing, which rules out that side.
- **Not tested:** index 12 (Ba 0.40), the Gaussian-process model's top pick, went unmeasured. I chose index 16 because the model predicted a higher average photocurrent there and a nearby phase has a very narrow gap. So the true peak could sit somewhere between Ba 0.40 and 0.46 rather than exactly at index 16. Mn-rich compositions below Ba 0.35 were not measured either; I skipped them only because the predicted gaps are narrow.

I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.
